title: Preferring Ellington and Horace Henderson to Fletcher Henderson
summary: He liked Ellington better than Fletcher Henderson and Horace Henderson's swing better still, disliking Fletcher's piano.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, did you get to hear Fletcher's band on record?
No, I -- Smack's
Mac's band was making good records by 1928.
Yes, he was making good records.
You didn't hear any good big bands on record, then.
That was after I finished high school.
Oh. When did you first hear Ellington?
I heard him on record. And --
Did that move you the same? It wasn't the same beat, was it?
His was a little different.
Yeah.
Much different.
Yeah, it wasn't up your alley quite the same way, huh?
Oh, I liked him better than I did Fletcher's band.
You did?
I sure did. It was something about --
Oh, you surprise me. That strange thing.
Right.
That mysterioso thing.
It's like, I like Fletcher's band. But I even liked Horace's band better, Horace Henderson.
Did you really?
Yes.
Because it was more of an out-and-out
swing band.
Yes, it played the -- it had more of a swing to it than Fletcher's.
Yeah, yeah.
Fletcher was a good arranger.
Yeah, but he didn't play piano the same way.
I guess that was it. His piano playing was different from Horace's.
It didn't have a drive to it, yeah.
Not like Horace's.
No, I know.
And that's why I liked Horace's band better.
Horace's band better, yeah.
Yeah.
Yeah.
But as far as his musicians and everything, he had good musicians. Fletch had good musicians. But I just didn't care much for his piano playing. That was the only thing.
Yeah, yeah.
